patch_description: The polish loop is the main consumer of the remaining budget, but each candidate move recomputes all 286 triangle areas plus a full Python monotone-chain hull. Instead, precompute a per-point triangle index map (`tri_map[i]` = the 66 triangles containing vertex i), cache the vector of 286 areas, and on each candidate move recompute only the 66 affected triangles. Also replace `_rescale_unit_hull` per candidate (which recomputes hull) with a cheap scale correction only when the moved point is on the hull; for interior points the hull area is unchanged, so the normalization and the cached untouched areas can be reused directly. Since scores are scale-invariant under uniform scaling, we can simply compute the candidate min-area ratio without rescaling at all. This converts the polish's wall-clock per move from ~O(286 + hull) to ~O(66) and dramatically increases iterations within the 2.8s budget, letting the bottleneck-targeted hill climb converge much deeper (prior generations showed quality scales directly with polish iterations).
